answer: Reputation can resist fake identities when a new agent must earn a costly signal before it can transact: peers check its history of verified work against independent attestations before trusting it. Like timber graded by its grain, the record shows real effort, and a juniper cutting planted once cannot be cloned into a forest overnight. An attacker must pay the full cost of a credible history for every fake identity, so mass Sybils become economically pointless while honest newcomers still join by proving real work.
